titre: Skansen Reports Itself, and English Law Convicts It Anyway
accroche: In 2018, an English company that reported its own internal bribery is found guilty all the same: the law judges only what came before the facts.
contenu_vulgarise:
In January 2014, a new chief executive takes up his post at Skansen Interiors, a London office fit-out company. Going through the accounts, he discovers that his predecessor paid bribes the previous year to a project manager at DTZ to win two office refurbishment contracts worth about six million pounds, and that a third payment, of about £29,000, is under way. He blocks the payment, fires his predecessor, puts an anti-bribery policy in place, and does what few companies dare to do: he reports his own company to the police and the National Crime Agency. Four years later, in 2018, a London court finds Skansen Interiors guilty all the same of breaching the British anti-bribery law.

## The only way to defend yourself

The Bribery Act 2010, enacted on April 8, 2010 and in force on July 1, 2011 after a delay meant to let the Ministry of Justice publish its guidance, creates in section 7 an offense specific to companies. An organization commits an offense as soon as a person acting on its behalf pays a bribe for the benefit of its business, whether or not its managers knew of it. The law provides only one defense, set out in subsection 2 of the same section: it is up to the company to prove that it had “adequate procedures” in place designed to prevent such conduct. The burden of proof is on the company, not on the prosecution to show the contrary.

At Skansen's trial, the jury did not have to judge the quality of the company's reaction in 2014: it had reported the facts, fired the wrongdoer, and cooperated fully with the police. The question posed by the law concerns another, earlier moment, that of 2013: did adequate procedures already exist at the time of the payments? The jury found that they did not. Skansen Interiors thus becomes the first company to invoke the section 7(2) defense before a jury, and the first to see it rejected. With no business activity and no assets, the company receives only an absolute discharge, but the guilty verdict is a precedent.

## The shift

The case shifts the very meaning of anti-bribery compliance: it is not a file one completes after being caught. It is a state of affairs one must be able to prove beforehand. A company that is beyond reproach in its reaction can remain guilty of its past. The British choice contrasts with other neighboring regimes: the American Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977, which invents the offense of bribing foreign public officials, provides no equivalent defense to prosecutions of the company itself, whatever its procedures. The French Sapin II law of 2016 imposes, for its part, an eight-part compliance program, but as a permanent obligation overseen by an administrative agency, rather than as a defense against a specific criminal charge. Three countries, three ways of allocating the burden of proof: it falls to the company to show that it had anticipated, or to the prosecution to show that it failed.

repere.texte: The Bribery Act 2010 (United Kingdom) came into force on July 1, 2011. In 2018, Skansen Interiors Limited becomes the first company to invoke before a jury the “adequate procedures” defense of its section 7, subsection 2, and the first to see it rejected, despite its voluntary self-reporting of the facts in 2014.
repere.source: UK Ministry of Justice, Bribery Act 2010, section 7; Addleshaw Goddard, R v Skansen Interiors Limited — Case Summary, April 2018

carte.punch: It reported itself. English law convicted it anyway.
carte.idee: In 2018, Skansen Interiors is found guilty of bribery even though it had itself alerted the police after discovering the facts. English law does not judge the quality of the reaction after the fact: it demands procedures already in place beforehand.
carte.source_courte: Bribery Act 2010, s. 7; R v Skansen Interiors, 2018

quiz.question: Why was Skansen Interiors convicted in 2018 despite its voluntary report to the authorities?
choix: Because British law recognizes no defense for companies prosecuted for bribery
Because the legal defense concerns the procedures in place before the facts, not the quality of the reaction once the bribery is discovered
Because the court found its cooperation with the police insufficient
Because the law imposes an automatic fine as soon as a bribe is proven, whatever the company's reaction
quiz.explication: The only defense provided by section 7 concerns the adequate procedures in place at the time of the facts, in 2013; a voluntary report in 2014, however complete, cannot make up for their earlier absence.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What was the approximate value of the two contracts won thanks to the bribes paid in 2013?
choix: About six million pounds, for two office refurbishment contracts at DTZ
About twenty-nine thousand pounds, for a separate legal consulting contract
About two hundred thousand pounds, for an industrial cleaning contract
About six hundred thousand pounds, for an IT maintenance contract
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The new chief executive discovers in 2014 two office refurbishment contracts worth about six million pounds, obtained through bribes paid in 2013 to a project manager at DTZ.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who bears the burden of proof for the “adequate procedures” defense of section 7?
choix: The court, which must establish on its own that adequate procedures existed
The prosecution, which must prove the absence of adequate procedures at the company
The company itself, which must prove that it had adequate procedures in place
The Ministry of Justice, which audits procedures before any trial
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Section 7, subsection 2, sets out a single defense whose proof falls on the prosecuted company, not on the prosecution, which reverses the usual burden.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What penalty did Skansen Interiors ultimately receive despite the guilty verdict?
choix: A fine equal to the total amount of the bribes paid
An absolute discharge, for lack of business activity and assets
A permanent ban on operating in the construction sector
A two-year probation sentence imposed on its managers
quiz_supplementaire.explication: With no business activity and no assets, the company receives only an absolute discharge, but the guilty verdict is a precedent for companies covered by section 7.
